name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
title: Pricing Illiquid Assets
answer: Pricing illiquid assets covers the valuation of holdings that do not trade on a public market, such as private company stakes, real estate, private credit, and stakes in funds that themselves hold hard to sell positions. In portfolio construction it matters because a portfolio's reported value and risk depend on prices that are estimated rather than observed. The work sits between accounting, valuation practice, and quantitative modelling, and it feeds directly into allocation, reporting, and performance measurement.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Pricing illiquid assets covers the valuation of holdings that do not trade on a public market, such as private company stakes, real estate, private credit, and stakes in funds that themselves hold hard to sell positions. In portfolio construction it matters because a portfolio's reported value and risk depend on prices that are estimated rather than observed. The work sits between accounting, valuation practice, and quantitative modelling, and it feeds directly into allocation, reporting, and performance measurement.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The inputs are usually a mix of deal data, comparable transactions, cash flow projections, and any observable prices from similar listed instruments. Systems range from spreadsheets and valuation platforms to data pipelines that pull filings, market quotes, and reference data into a single store. This site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which can serve as comparables when a private holding has a listed peer, though the mapping is rarely exact.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners typically triangulate several approaches: market multiples from comparable companies or transactions, discounted cash flow using projected earnings, and cost or recent round pricing for early stage positions. Models are adjusted for size, growth, leverage, and lack of marketability, and the result is often a range rather than a single number. Machine learning is used mainly to screen comparables, fill gaps in sparse data, and flag outliers, not to replace the judgement of a valuer.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Valuation is governed by accounting standards, fund documents, and internal valuation policies, with independent review and committee sign off for the largest or most uncertain positions. Provenance matters: the source of each input, the date it was captured, and the assumptions behind the model must be documented and auditable.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward more frequent, more transparent marks, with automation handling data collection and first pass estimates while humans own the final call. Private market growth and the rise of retail access to illiquid funds are pushing valuation toward daily or monthly reporting rather than quarterly. Expect tighter documentation requirements and more use of listed proxies, though the gap between an estimate and a true exit price will remain.
